Richer flavor and noticeably bigger prawns. ``` ```menu { "title": "Spicy Beef Tendon Soup", "rating": 4 } --- Similar to Korean galbitang but with a slightly sour broth — might be hit or miss depending on your taste. ``` ## Review After the tour ended, I picked the most appealing spot from the guide's restaurant recommendations. It was cold and I was craving something exotic with a warm broth. Song Fa Bak Kut Teh from Singapore came to mind, and I figured a Thai restaurant would have something in a similar vein. It's located in a basement, but once inside it was surprisingly spacious. The robot serving system was a cool modern touch. ```adcard ``` Orders are placed via QR code at the table and payment is handled instantly — no language barrier at all. The only slightly annoying part was having to register a card upfront before paying. `Travel Wallet` cards are supported, and if registering is too much hassle, you can request a separate payment at the counter. The Pad Thai was the richest and most flavorful I've ever had. The local prawns were big and plump — probably why. The Spicy Beef Tendon Soup tasted familiar, like Korean galbitang, but with a slightly sour edge to the broth. It didn't bother me at all — I actually liked it. Still not sure why it's called ```Spicy```. Overall a satisfying meal. It's a large 150-seat restaurant that's popular with Thai locals too. ## Pictures
